subject: chemistry
title: Chemical Bonding & Structure Adventure 1: Ionic and covalent bonding
welcome_lead: Today you'll lose, share or pool electrons — ionic, covalent and metallic bonds.
meta_desc: IBDP Chemistry — ionic, covalent (polar and non-polar), metallic bonding, properties.
final_note: You learned ionic = transfer giving lattice, covalent = shared pair (polar if electronegativity differs), metallic = sea of delocalised e⁻.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Metal + non-metal: electrons transfer.

Na (1 valence e⁻) loses → Na⁺; Cl (7 valence e⁻) gains → Cl⁻. Lattice held by electrostatic attraction.

Properties: high mp, conduct when molten or aqueous, brittle, often soluble in water.

Non-metal + non-metal: electrons shared.

H₂, Cl₂, CO₂, H₂O.

Polarity: if ΔEN > 0, bond is polar. C-O is polar (δ⁺C-Oδ⁻).
Molecule is polar if dipoles don't cancel. CO₂ linear → non-polar; H₂O bent → polar.

Metal cations sit in a sea of delocalised electrons.

Explains:
- Electrical conductivity (e⁻ free to move).
- Malleability (cations slide past one another).
- High mp (strong attraction).

Bond strength: charge density (Mg²⁺ > Na⁺), explaining mp Mg > Na.
